To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the development process for a control system can be formalized, and the formalized process can be used to record the assumptions made about the environment of the control system.
the specification of the environment can be used to derive a specification for the control system and that this can be used in a development process to obtain a program.

the specification of an open system can be determined by the specification of its environment and that the specification of a system and that of its environment together determine the specification of a controller.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of methods and tools that allow a system designer to specify the behaviour of a system, and its environment, in a way which is sufficiently precise to allow a computer program to be generated from it.
developing a method for deriving the specification of a closed-loop control system from a specification of its environment.

-the formal specification of the behaviour of a class of open systems, and in particular the development of methods for deriving the specification of the control system from that of the environment; -the use of such specifications as a means of documenting assumptions about the physical world, and of identifying the kinds of errors which the system may make in that world; -the use in this way of specifications as an aid to the design of reliable control systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the specification of a system can be derived from the specification of the environment, and the specification of the system is a function of that of the environment.
the system is correct with respect to a given specification and the assumptions made.
the specification of the physical world is the same as the specification of the system, and vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specification of the environment of a control system can be determined by the specification of the system itself.
we have developed a formal method for deriving the specification of the controller from that of the physical system and its environment.
we have shown the feasibility of a new approach to specifying control systems, and have demonstrated the benefits of using this approach in practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to specify the behaviour of a control system, we should also specify the behaviour of its environment, in a way which is precise enough to be used in reasoning about the system.
the specification of the environment of a system is a critical part of the system's specification.
the specification of a system should be a statement about the world it interacts with.
